data.name: Dr. Bulbaceous
data.detailed_description:
A Puzzling Arcade Experience.

Descend through 100 levels of challenging puzzle mayhem in a quest to defeat the big bad boss at the bottom of the bottom most well. Fans of Uo Poko, Puzzle Bubble and Bust-a-move will enjoy Dr. B or be prosecutedt to the full extent of the jam.




As Dr. B, you have the official task of cleaning the wells of Bulbville by matching 3 or more bulbs of the same colour. If you play well, you get Cookies that allow you to "cheat" by buying strange balls from the Swap Shop but by using these balls to clear a well, you get less cookies for each level cleared. What do you do?!

There is, of course, an end of level boss waiting for you down the dankest level of the 100th well but don't tell them I said that!



  • Runs on Linux, Windows & Mac
  • 100 levels of well designed puzzling puzzles
  • Levels get progressively strange but varies in difficulty
  • Features more than 20 balls of varying powers & effects
  • Features just the one mode - HARDCORE
  • Surprise end of level boss
  • Hypnotic physics simulator engine
  • Your choice of strategy or grind
  • Cookies are always returned when game ends so spend away or not at all
  • Forgiving level system where you can buy back levels when your game ends
  • Dynamic in-game soundtrack for full effect



Built in lua using our open source engine, GameCake.

reviews.review:
Developed and published by Wetgenes, Dr. Bulbaceous is a colorful arcade puzzle game that pays tribute to the timeless bubble-matching formula while introducing a few ideas of its own to keep players engaged over the course of a surprisingly lengthy adventure. The game follows the eccentric Dr. Bulbaceous as he ventures into the underground wells of Bulbville, clearing clusters of vibrant bulbs while making his way toward a final confrontation hidden at the bottom of a one-hundred-level campaign. Its premise is intentionally simple, placing the emphasis squarely on satisfying gameplay instead of an elaborate narrative, but the cheerful presentation and quirky personality give the experience enough charm to stand apart from many similar puzzle releases.

The gameplay revolves around launching colored bulbs to create groups of three or more matching colors, causing them to disappear before the screen becomes overcrowded. While this familiar mechanic is easy to understand within minutes, the game steadily increases the challenge by introducing more demanding layouts and requiring greater accuracy as players descend deeper into the wells. Every successful shot becomes more rewarding as the difficulty rises, encouraging careful planning rather than random firing. The gradual progression feels well balanced, allowing newcomers to build confidence before facing the tougher stages that require quicker reactions and smarter decision-making.

One of the game's more distinctive features is its Cookie reward system. Completing levels earns Cookies that can be spent in the Swap Shop to purchase special bulbs capable of helping players overcome difficult situations. These power-ups provide useful tactical advantages, but relying on them comes with a meaningful tradeoff by reducing the number of Cookies earned upon clearing a stage. This creates a satisfying balance between conserving resources and using them when absolutely necessary. Instead of functioning as an easy shortcut, the system encourages strategic thinking and resource management, giving experienced players another layer of depth beyond simply matching colors.

The lengthy one hundred-level campaign gives Dr. Bulbaceous more substance than many arcade-style puzzle games that focus solely on endless score chasing. Reaching the deepest levels becomes a genuine accomplishment, especially with the promise of a boss encounter waiting at the end of the journey. The increasing challenge keeps the experience engaging without feeling unfair, rewarding players who learn to read the board efficiently and make the most of every shot. Each completed level contributes to a satisfying sense of progression, making it easy to lose track of time while attempting to push just a little farther.

Presentation is another area where the game succeeds despite its modest production values. The colorful cartoon visuals match the lighthearted tone perfectly, creating an inviting atmosphere that complements the accessible gameplay. The bulb designs are easy to distinguish, animations remain smooth, and the environments maintain a playful style throughout the adventure. Audio also fits the game's arcade roots, with energetic music and satisfying sound effects that reinforce every successful chain reaction. The interface is straightforward and easy to navigate, while support for controllers, Steam Achievements, Trading Cards, Cloud Saves, and online leaderboards provides additional incentives for players who enjoy replaying stages or competing for higher scores.

Although the game remains entertaining throughout its campaign, its reliance on a traditional puzzle formula means some players may eventually experience a sense of repetition, particularly if they are looking for significant gameplay variety or a deeper storyline. The mechanics evolve gradually rather than dramatically, making the experience feel intentionally old-school. However, this commitment to classic arcade design is also one of its greatest strengths. Players who appreciate skill-based puzzle games built around precision, consistency, and steadily increasing difficulty will likely find the straightforward approach refreshing instead of limiting.

Dr. Bulbaceous ultimately delivers exactly what it promises: a polished and enjoyable arcade puzzle experience inspired by genre classics while adding enough original mechanics to establish its own identity. The Cookie economy, rewarding progression, charming presentation, and satisfying challenge combine into a game that remains engaging from its opening stages through its final descent into Bulbville's depths. It may not redefine the bubble-matching genre, but it demonstrates how thoughtful design and solid gameplay fundamentals can still create a compelling experience. Fans of classic puzzle games looking for a lengthy single-player adventure with accessible mechanics and lasting replay value should find plenty to appreciate here.

Rating: 7/10
